# a rule

```
rule: cma1990.s2
extent: E.W. S.
section: 2
written by: Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-10-30, standing in for the small model (Luna or Haiku) of the chain
  legislation -> small model -> SLAM -> Reasoned Thought; not yet written by that model
source: Computer Misuse Act 1990, section 2(1) and (2), https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/18/section/2
```

person: a thing that can know, can say what it can do, and can do it
law: a list of rules for each person
element: a part of a rule that has to be true
elements: more than one element
offence: a thing that a rule says a person can not do
evidence: data that says an element is true or false
intends: makes one thing so that an other thing is the result
help: do a part of a thing for a person, so that the person can do it
further: an other one, after the first
sentence: what a rule of the law says a person has to get for an offence
fixed: set, so that it can not change
years: a way to count time
three: the number after two
four: the number after three
five: the number after four
writes: makes words in a thing
record: data that a computer or a person writes at the time of a thing
event: a thing at a place and a time, that a record or a person can say is so
kind: a name for a set of things that are the same in one way
about: a word for what a thing is for
section: a part of a law, with a number
does: a word for do, for one person or thing
commits: does

it is about an event of kind:

```
CREDENTIAL_USED
```

the law, as code:

```
(1) A person is guilty of an offence under this section if he commits an offence under section 1 above ("the unauthorised access offence") with intent—
(a) to commit an offence to which this section applies; or
(b) to facilitate the commission of such an offence (whether by himself or by any other person); and the offence he intends to commit or facilitate is referred to below in this section as the further offence.
(2) This section applies to offences—
(a) for which the sentence is fixed by law; or
(b) for which a person who has attained the age of twenty-one years (eighteen in relation to England and Wales) and has no previous convictions may be sentenced to imprisonment for a term of five years (or, in England and Wales, might be so sentenced but for the restrictions imposed by section 33 of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980).
```

element 1:

```
he commits an offence under section 1 above
```

the person commits the offence of section 1, with each element of it true.

it is the offence:

```
cma1990.s1
```

element 2:

```
to commit an offence to which this section applies
```

```
to facilitate the commission of such an offence (whether by himself or by any other person)
```

the person intends to do a further offence, or to help a person to do it.

it takes evidence of:

```
INTENT_FURTHER_OFFENCE
```

element 3:

```
for which the sentence is fixed by law
```

```
may be sentenced to imprisonment for a term of five years
```

for the further offence, the law has a sentence that is fixed, or a sentence of five years or more.

it takes evidence of:

```
MAXIMUM_SENTENCE
```

rule: when element 1, element 2 and element 3 are true, the offence is true.
